title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Texas Tech traditions, from game-day signals and mascots to campus bells, songs, and the annual lighting ceremony.

cards.title: Guns Up
cards.subtitle: The Red Raider greeting and victory sign
cards.notes: Use the hand sign as a greeting or during athletics, following the university’s described finger-and-thumb formation.
cards.short_summary: A Red Raider hand sign adopted as a campus tradition in 1971.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech identifies Guns Up as the widely recognized Red Raider greeting and a victory sign used at athletic events; it says the tradition began in 1971.
cards.access_notes: A gesture used at events and as a greeting; no special access is required to make it.

cards.title: The Masked Rider’s home-game run
cards.subtitle: Mounted mascot entrance at Texas Tech home games
cards.notes: Arrive before kickoff to watch the masked student rider, in cape and mask, lead the team onto the field.
cards.short_summary: Texas Tech’s official mounted mascot has led the team onto the field since 1954.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech states that the Masked Rider became an official mascot in 1954 and today leads the team onto the field for home games.
cards.access_notes: Watch from an authorized game-day seat or event viewing area; athletic-event admission may apply.

cards.title: Raider Red appearances
cards.subtitle: Texas Tech’s costumed public-relations mascot
cards.notes: Look for the costumed mascot at a listed athletics event or campus appearance, and keep interactions respectful.
cards.short_summary: A costumed mascot created in 1971 as an alternative to the mounted Masked Rider.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech says Saddle Tramp Jim Gaspard created Raider Red from a Dirk West drawing as an alternative to the Masked Rider.
cards.access_notes: Appearance locations vary by event; athletic-event admission may apply.

cards.title: Sing the Matador Song
cards.subtitle: Texas Tech’s alma mater
cards.notes: Learn the alma mater before a formal university occasion or athletics event so you can join the song appropriately.
cards.short_summary: The university’s alma mater pairs words by R.C. Marshall with music by Harry Lemaire.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech identifies the Matador Song as its alma mater, with music by Harry Lemaire and words by R.C. Marshall.
cards.access_notes: The lyrics are publicly available on the university traditions page.

cards.title: “Fight, Raiders, Fight!”
cards.subtitle: The Texas Tech fight song
cards.notes: Follow the printed lyrics at a sporting event and listen for the final line that calls out the Victory Bells.
cards.short_summary: Carroll McMath wrote the fight song that names the scarlet and black and Victory Bells.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech credits Carroll McMath with its Fight Song and publishes its lyrics, including the reference to the Victory Bells.
cards.access_notes: The lyrics are publicly available; attendance costs depend on the particular sporting event.

cards.title: Carol of Lights® switch-on
cards.subtitle: Annual holiday ceremony in the Science Quadrangle
cards.notes: Check the campus-events page before attending; the ceremony includes music and the campus-lighting moment in the Science Quadrangle.
cards.short_summary: An annual December lighting ceremony that illuminates campus buildings for the holiday season.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech’s 2026 event page lists Carol of Lights® for December 6 in the Science Quadrangle and says more than 30,000 lights illuminate campus.
cards.source_title: The 67th Annual Carol of Lights | Campus Events | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for December 6, 2026, with a 6:30 p.m. carillon concert and 7 p.m. ceremony; confirm details before going.

cards.title: Bangin’ Bertha
cards.subtitle: The Saddle Tramps’ trailer-mounted bell
cards.notes: Spot the named bell at a home football game or homecoming event; leave ringing it to the Saddle Tramps.
cards.short_summary: A 1959 bell, designed by a Saddle Tramp and donated by the Santa Fe Railroad.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech says Saddle Tramps carry Bangin’ Bertha to home football games and homecoming events; the bell was designed in 1959 by Joe Winegar.
cards.source_title: Bangin' Bertha (Saddle Tramp Bell) | History & Traditions | TTU
cards.access_notes: Appears at home football games and homecoming events; event admission or access rules may apply.

cards.title: Victory Bells
cards.subtitle: Administration Building east tower
cards.notes: Listen after a Texas Tech victory or special occasion; the university assigns bell-ringing to the Saddle Tramps.
cards.short_summary: Two bells, given as the Class of 1936 gift, mark victories and special occasions.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech says Saddle Tramps ring the Victory Bells after victories and special occasions; the 1,200-pound pair hangs in the Administration Building’s east tower.
cards.access_notes: The bells are university-managed and not for public operation; observe from public campus areas.

cards.title: Old Will wrapped in red
cards.subtitle: Saddle Tramp ritual before home football games
cards.notes: View the Will Rogers and Soapsuds statue near Memorial Circle before a home game; do not touch or add material to it.
cards.short_summary: Saddle Tramps wrap the campus statue in red crepe paper before every home football game.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech states that Saddle Tramps wrap the Will Rogers and Soapsuds statue with red crepe paper before every home football game.
cards.source_title: Will Rogers & Soapsuds | History & Traditions | TTU
cards.access_notes: View the outdoor landmark from public walkways; do not climb, touch, or alter the statue.

cards.title: The pre-kickoff Bell Circle
cards.subtitle: Saddle Tramps’ football kickoff formation
cards.notes: Be in the stadium before kickoff to see the Saddle Tramps form the Bell Circle; follow venue and staff directions.
cards.short_summary: A Saddle Tramp pre-kickoff ritual documented by the university alongside bell ringing and campus-event service.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech describes the Saddle Tramps as forming the “Bell Circle” moments before football kickoff, alongside their other tradition-keeping roles.
cards.access_notes: Visible during football pregame from authorized stadium seating; game admission may apply.
